messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT PAGER: high error rate for VortexCorp private VPC egress -> 504s from NLB targets. Severity: P2. Runbook: vpc-egress-failures. Paging oncall: @mike (oncall)  

mike (oncall): Ack. I'm on it. Any customer notes? Are they impacted externally?  

olga (customer-eng): Customer reports API calls from their app failing intermittently for ~10m. They see: 'upstream reset' and DNS timeouts on service discovery to our NLB. Impacting 20% of requests.  

jess (net-ops): Observed spike in TCP RSTs from targets behind the private NLB. NLB healthchecks are flapping for some targets in the Vortex dedicated pool. Also seeing a drop in SNAT ephemeral ports on the tenant NAT instance.  

anna (eng-runtime): Throwing in telemetry: request latency up, 95th p50->4s p95->12s, token generation queues growing. No model runtime OOMs. Looks like requests are failing upstream at the network boundary.  

mike (oncall): OK—prioritize isolation: is this per-tenant or cluster-wide?  

jess (net-ops): Narrowed to Vortex dedicated pool + their VPC NAT instance. Other tenants on same region unaffected. Likely conntrack / ephemeral port exhaustion + security-group churn.  

lin (solutions): Customer recently applied a security team change? I had a sync this morning; they asked for tightened SG egress on fw rules. Could be related.  

olga (customer-eng): Confirmed: they pushed a security group rule at 09:10 that tightened outbound to outbound ports 443 only and limited destination prefixes. They say it should still allow our NLB, but maybe CIDR mismatch.  

jess (net-ops): Can we get a quick rule dump?  

olga (customer-eng): Paste from their console: ```
SecurityGroup sg-0vtx
Outbound:
 - Allow TCP 443 -> 10.12.0.0/20
 - Deny 0.0.0.0/0 (default)```

jess (net-ops): Aha — our NLB has IPs in 10.12.32.0/24 (outside their allowed range). That would block new connections and break healthchecks.  

mike (oncall): That explains it. So customer-side SG is too restrictive. What's fastest mitigation path?  

anna (eng-runtime): Options:
 - Ask customer to expand SG (fast if they approve) -> long term fix.
 - Add temporary proxy/egress NAT in permitted CIDR that routes to NLB -> infra work but we can do short-term NAT translation.
 - Failover to a compatible dedicated pool in same region that matches allowed CIDR -> requires provisioning and possibly model warmup.

lin (solutions): Customer prefers we do the short-term change to avoid their internal change window. They asked if we can NAT from 10.12.15.0/24 which is in their allowed range.  

jess (net-ops): We can stand up a managed NAT gateway in their VPC with an IP from that prefix and SNAT outbound to the NLB. Quick steps:
 - create transit ENI with IP 10.12.15.23
 - add route to direct egress to NAT
 - update NLB target security to accept connections from 10.12.15.0/24
This will take ~20-30m + tests.  

mike (oncall): Estimate risk? Are there any cross-tenant exposure concerns?  

jess (net-ops): Low risk — NAT will be in their VPC and traffic stays within private links. We'll ensure the NAT only has routes to the NLB endpoints. We'll also temporarily scope SG on our side to accept only that IP range.  

anna (eng-runtime): We'll set model warmup on the fallback pool if needed. Also prepare a rollback plan: if NAT route misbehaves, remove route and fallback to customer expanded SG.  

mike (oncall): OK proceed with managed NAT + SG whitelisting. Keep updates here. @olga keep customer informed and get sign-off for the temporary NAT IP.  

olga (customer-eng): Got it. Asking customer for sign-off now. ETA 5–10m.  

[5m later]

olga (customer-eng): Customer approved 10.12.15.23 as temporary egress IP. Proceed.  

jess (net-ops): Starting provisioning. Command snippet:
```
# create transit ENI
aws ec2 create-network-interface --subnet-id subnet-0abc --private-ip-address 10.12.15.23 --group-ids sg-allow-nat
# attach, configure iptables SNAT -> 10.12.15.23
```

[10m later]

jess (net-ops): ENI up, SNAT applied, updated route table. Pinging NLB endpoints -> successful from NAT. Updating our target SG to accept 10.12.15.0/24.  

anna (eng-runtime): Starting controlled warmups for Vortex models on the dedicated pool.  

mike (oncall): Rolling small percentage of traffic to NAT path now. Watch metrics.  

anna (eng-runtime): Telemetry: error rate dropping from 20% -> 4% after initial traffic ramp. p95 latency back to ~800ms for flows through NAT.  

olga (customer-eng): Customer reports successful test calls. They still see occasional failures but much improved.  

lin (solutions): Noted: because this is temporary, add annotation to the runbook and create an action item for the customer to expand allowed CIDR or use our published NLB range.  

mike (oncall): Agreed. I'll create a follow-up ticket to coordinate permanent SG update and to schedule a cutover test with customer.  

jess (net-ops): Leaving NAT in place for now. We'll monitor conntrack and NAT metrics; will expire after 24h unless we get permanent SG change.  

mike (oncall): Fine. Handoff to daytime oncall @tara (day-oncall) in 10m with list of actions.  

tara (day-oncall): Ack. I'll take over monitoring, notify SRE rotation, and chase the customer for permanent SG adjustment. Please drop runbook link and ticket id.  

mike (oncall): Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/vpc-egress-failures
Follow-up ticket: RWF-8123 (customer SG update + postmortem).  

olga (customer-eng): Customer requested a short postmortem once fully resolved. I'll schedule joint RCA.  

mike (oncall): Closing pager for now — condition improved, mitigation in place. Leaving thread open for handoff notes and PM updates. :white_check_mark:  

[end of thread]
